cards.text: Jesus enters the town of Jericho, and He's passing through. And there's a man in Jericho named Zacchaeus.

cards.question: Zacchaeus has a big title. What is he?

cards.text: Chief tax collector, VERY wealthy. And I bet all that money can't help him with what he's trying to do: see who Jesus is.

cards.question: Zacchaeus can't see Jesus because Jesus has already gone by.

cards.text: Nope, there's a crowd, and Zacchaeus is small in stature. Friend, I'm a cookie stamper who spent YEARS looking up at mixing bowls like they were mountains, so I FEEL this.

cards.question: Zacchaeus runs on ahead and climbs a ___ tree to see Jesus.
Zacchaeus climbs the sycamore tree because Jesus is about to pass that way.

cards.text: Jesus comes to that spot, looks up, calls Zacchaeus by name and tells him to hurry down. Friend, you climb a tree just to get a LOOK, and the One everybody came to see looks STRAIGHT UP at YOU.

cards.question: Jesus tells Zacchaeus to hurry down out of the sycamore tree. What reason does Jesus give?

answers.text: He must stay at his house today
The crowd is about to block the road
He has a message for all of Jericho

cards.question: Zacchaeus hurries down from the tree and welcomes Jesus ___.
When the people see Jesus go to Zacchaeus's house, every one of them is happy about it.
All who saw Jesus go with Zacchaeus begin to grumble. What do they say?

answers.text: He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man
He has gone to be the guest of a Pharisee
He has passed by the rest of Jericho

cards.text: The whole crowd is grumbling. But Zacchaeus stands up and speaks to the Lord, and friend, I did NOT see this coming.

cards.question: What does Zacchaeus tell the Lord he gives to the poor?
Zacchaeus says that if he has cheated anyone, he will repay it ___.

cards.text: HALF of his stuff and FOUR times back? Friend, when I burn one cookie, I bake ONE more and call it even, and I'm PROUD of myself.

cards.question: Jesus tells Zacchaeus that today ___ has come to this house.
Jesus says salvation has come to Zacchaeus's house today. What reason does He give?

answers.text: This man too is a son of Abraham
This man has kept the whole law
This man was first to see Me

cards.text: Then Jesus says what the Son of Man came to do. Friend, I spent years lost in the back of a junk drawer, so lean in, because this line is the whole passage in one sentence.

cards.question: Jesus says the Son of Man came to ___ and to ___ the lost.

findings.problem: Zacchaeus first appears on card 1 by name only, with no simple description of who he is. Card 2 then asks what he is, so the walkthrough is built on the missing introduction. Card 1 should introduce him (for example as a chief tax collector), and card 2 should ask something else.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The opening card is a flat summary with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Only cards 5 and 16 try for a laugh. Cards 1, 3 and 13 read like a pleasant narrator, not like a laugh-out-loud funny one, even where the moment could hold a real laugh, such as a wealthy official climbing a tree.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: "The One everybody came to see" says why the crowd was there. Luke 19:3 only says there was a crowd Zacchaeus couldn't see over.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: "The whole crowd is grumbling" stretches Luke 19:7, which says "all who saw this" began to grumble. That group is not necessarily the whole crowd.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card retells the grumbling from Luke 19:7 but cites only Luke 19:8. It should cite Luke 19:7-8.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card only repeats the answers to cards 14 and 15 (half his possessions, fourfold) and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't share the core action. Zacchaeus is repaying people he may have cheated. Replacing a burnt cookie wrongs no one and repays no one, so the joke doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Many choice cards can only be answered by luck. Cards 2, 6, 9, 14, 15 and 18 have no story-card context the baker can reason from. For example, card 13 sets up Zacchaeus speaking but says nothing about money, the poor or making things right before cards 14 and 15. Discovery questions make up about half the stop, which is more than a few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: With two blanks, deciding which right word goes in which blank (seek first, save second) tests exact wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning. "Teach" also fits the line plausibly. The card asks the baker to guess the words of the verse.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
